messages.text: Can you redraw the sectoral views for Si-W and LAr prototypes now that sparked this discussions about different radii, I would like to see it now with the updated LAr prototype, but still show/illustrate the difference between Si-W and LAr for particle passing (as we had before)
I’ll redraw the same sector comparison using the updated 1.8 mm Pb LAr model, keeping the Si–W sector gap and the inclined LAr crossings clear and to scale.

I found the previous native DD4hep slice renderer. I’ll reuse its unchanged Si–W view and regenerate the LAr view from the exact geometry used in the restored 10k run. Both panels will share axes and scale. I’m using the repository’s design/validation workflow and rechecking the native runtime before extraction.

The Spack fingerprint warning persists, so I’ll verify the runtime before using it. The LAr panel will show sampling radii **1.773–2.350 m** and warm outer radius **2.642 m**, with the inclined Pb/LAr layers and comparison ray drawn from the native geometry.

The updated layout will now be shown at the same physical scale in both panels, including the close-ups. That makes the key difference visible: the Si–W structural seam stays aligned radially, while a straight particle path crosses the inclined LAr sampling gaps.

The native slices are regenerated. Along the marked particle path, Si–W has no sensitive crossings at the seam; the updated LAr model has 110 sensitive path segments. The close-ups now cover exactly the same XY window. I’ll package the drawing with SVG/PDF exports and the geometry provenance.

The redraw is saved in [draft PR #149](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/149), with SVG, PNG and PDF exports. It shows the LAr sampling region at 1.773–2.350 m and the vessel extending to 2.642 m, while preserving the earlier Si–W comparison. I’m finishing the independent check and repository records.

The figure and exports are complete, and the local project, provenance and accounting checks pass. The drawing makes the passage difference clear: the marked ray stays in the inactive Si–W seam, while the inclined LAr gaps cut across it repeatedly.

The independent review found no material scientific or visual issue. It confirmed the updated LAr dimensions, preserved Si–W geometry, matched scales and native crossing counts. I’m saving that review and the final records alongside the drawing.
